Pairs Rules

A quick reference for how PaperGames plays Pairs, the card-matching game.

The basic idea

The cards
All cards lie face down, and every shape appears on exactly two of them. You choose the size: 4 x 3 (6 pairs), 4 x 4 (8 pairs), 6 x 4 (12 pairs) or 6 x 6 (18 pairs).
A turn
On your turn, turn over two cards, one after the other. If they show the same shape, you take the pair and go again. If not, both are turned face down again and it is the other player's turn.
Nothing turns back by itself
Both cards stay face up as long as you like - there is no timer. Only your next tap, anywhere on the board, turns two cards that don't match back over. The same goes for the computer's cards: they stay open until you tap.

Who plays

Solo
Find all pairs on your own, in as few moves as you can. A move is one turn of two cards.
Two players
Two players share one device and take turns. Whoever has taken more pairs at the end wins; with the same number it is a draw.
Against the computer
Easy remembers nothing and turns cards over at random. Medium remembers the last six cards it has seen. Hard remembers every card that has ever been face up and never forgets one, so it is very hard to beat.

How a game ends

The end
The game ends when the last pair has been taken.
